answer.markdown:
Personalization pays in food tech, but less than vendors claim: 5–15% revenue lift in retail and only 1–2% in grocery[^a2c6][^a2c17], and the money is now made in retail media[^a2c11].

## The lift is real, and small in grocery

McKinsey puts the revenue lift at 5–15% across retail, but only 1–2% of total sales for grocers[^a2c6][^a2c17].

**Revenue lift from personalization**

Grocery's 1–2% sits well below the broad-retail range, and the vendor figures sit far above it[^a2c17][^a2c4].

| | Revenue lift from personalization | Scope | Sources |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Retail, all categories | 5–15% | McKinsey · revenue | [^a2c6] |
| Grocery | 1–2% | McKinsey · total sales | [^a2c17] |
| Starbucks | 4–6% | same-store sales · 2023–24 | [^a2c4] |
| Domino's | 63% | revenue growth · several initiatives | [^a2c9] |

## Vendor figures do not survive a filing

Starbucks' $2.1B and Domino's 63% appear only in marketing analyses, not in either company's reports[^a2c4][^a2c9].

**How big is the revenue lift from personalization?**

The large vendor figures could not be traced to a filing[^a2c4].

| | How big is the revenue lift from personalization? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Benchmarks (leaning) · primary | 1–2% | McKinsey puts the grocery lift at 1–2% of total sales[^a2c17]. |
| Vendor case studies · seo | $2.1B | Starbucks' $2.1B and Domino's 63% come from marketing write-ups[^a2c4][^a2c9]. |

Would settle it: A Starbucks 10-K or earnings call that attributes revenue to Deep Brew.

## The money is retail media, not data sales

Kroger's 84.51° says purchase-based targeting drove 4x the sales uplift with 50% fewer impressions[^a2c11].

**Advertising revenue**

All three platforms report billion-dollar ad businesses, on different bases[^a2c12][^a2c13].

| | Advertising revenue | As of | Scope | Sources |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Uber | >$2B | 2026-Q1 | annualized run rate | [^a2c13] |
| Instacart | >$1B | 2025 | ads and other, full year | [^a2c12] |
| DoorDash | >$1B ⚠ not in quote | 2024 | ads, full year | [^a2c18] |

## Diet data is policed by enforcement, not HIPAA

Most diet and delivery apps sit outside HIPAA, so the FTC acts as the de facto health-data regulator[^a3c5][^a3c6].

The FTC has gone as far as ordering WW and Kurbo to destroy the algorithms built on children's data[^a3c7].

Most figures come from company reports and vendor write-ups rather than filings[^a2c4].

A contextual bandit dynamically allocates retrieval slots across candidate sources under a fixed compute budget.
Rule-based filtering for allergies and seasonality achieved 100% precision in technical validation.
Contextual-bandit algorithms address the cold-start problem by exploring with non-personalized, popular items before adapting to the user.

Personalized push notifications sent before mealtimes lifted orders by 28% compared with generic messages.
Deep Brew is credited with an estimated $2.1 billion in incremental revenue from AI-driven personalized recommendations between 2023 and 2024, with same-store sales up 4-6% in channels using it.
Personalization can reduce acquisition costs by as much as 50 percent, lift revenues by 5 to 15 percent, and increase the efficiency of marketing spend by 10 to 30 percent.
Win-back campaigns lifted reactivation to 14% and cut re-acquisition CAC by about 22% versus new-user spend.

On March 4, 2022 the FTC's settlement required WW International and Kurbo to delete illegally collected data from children, destroy any algorithms derived from it, and pay a $1.5 million penalty.
